text: Walk into almost any enterprise that's been on-prem for a decade and then adopted Azure and AWS, and you'll find three separate places where 'who is this person' gets answered. Nobody designed that on purpose — it's what happens when each environment got adopted on its own timeline. This lesson is about turning three identities into one.

A new hire ends up with an on-prem AD account for their domain-joined laptop, a Microsoft Entra ID account for Microsoft 365 and Azure, and — if their job touches AWS — a separate AWS identity nobody remembered to connect. Three accounts means three passwords, three MFA enrollments, and the part that actually gets companies breached: three offboarding steps. Disable someone in AD, and their AWS access can keep working for months.

Microsoft Entra Connect fixes the on-prem-to-Azure half. It's a sync agent that reads your Active Directory and writes matching user and group objects into Entra ID on a schedule, so one person is now represented consistently in two places. You get a real choice for passwords: Password Hash Sync lets Entra ID validate sign-ins on its own, while Pass-through Authentication keeps the actual check on-prem through a lightweight agent. Add Seamless SSO, and a domain-joined machine signs in without a visible prompt at all.

Entra Connect alone does nothing for AWS, and giving AWS its own synced copy of AD would just recreate the same problem one level up. The right move is AWS IAM Identity Center, which acts as a SAML service provider trusting Entra ID as the identity provider. Microsoft even publishes a ready-made gallery app for it — exchange SAML metadata once, and a user already signed into Entra ID lands in AWS without a separate password. SCIM provisioning keeps the right users and groups flowing into AWS automatically, including removing them the moment they leave.

That's the pattern: one hybrid identity, extended — not duplicated — into every cloud it needs to reach. Next lesson goes deeper into how that federation actually works for a true multi-cloud org, including how Entra ID groups map to real AWS permissions.
